title: Database Query Optimization
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of database query optimization and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn database query optimization through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Database Query Optimization matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines database query optimization as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Query count analysis; QuerySet.explain(); Related-object loading; Indexing; Avoiding unnecessary data retrieval. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Query count analysis
items.text: Query count analysis should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: QuerySet.explain()
items.text: A QuerySet describes database operations and is commonly lazy. Build filters and ordering before evaluation; use the database to narrow results rather than pulling everything into Python.

items.title: Related-object loading
items.text: For Related-object loading, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Indexing
items.text: Indexing should be evaluated using a representative workload and a measured baseline. Compare correctness and resource usage before and after the change; the best choice depends on the database backend, request mix and data size.

items.title: Avoiding unnecessary data retrieval
items.text: Avoiding unnecessary data retrieval affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.
